lines.text: Why will you never see a square window on a plane?
The first jet airliner had big, nearly square windows.
Vik bets a week of desserts that round windows are just for looks.
But this jet flew higher than any airliner before, so every flight pumped the cabin up like a balloon.
Within two years, two of them broke apart in the sky.
So engineers sank a whole plane in a water tank and pumped it up and down, again and again.
Until it burst, and the crack started at a sharp corner.
That's when Gus cuts a square hole and a round hole in paper, and pulls.
The square tears at the corner. The round one holds.
You see, a sharp corner squeezes all the stress into one tiny point, but a curve spreads it all the way around.
So every plane since has rounded windows.
And Vik's square brownie? It cracks right at the corner.
So next time you fly, look out and ask…
